mostWorthwhile.text: Building the epidermal barrier was most worthwhile: the planned cross-section and explanation connect lipids and outer cells to reduced water loss and renewal from deeper layers.

leastWorthwhile.text: The failed attempt to join the epidermis directly to connective tissue was confusing: the visible descriptions suggested adjacent layers, but did not explain why the dermis first needed vessels.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the epidermal barrier could not initially combine with anything; vascularising the dermis first made the layer combination possible.

arbitrary.text: Requiring blood vessels in the dermis before joining the layers felt somewhat arbitrary, even though a vascular dermis has a clear biological role.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter: connecting the skin's barrier, glands, vessels and nerves to the existing body was useful, although the required assembly order was occasionally opaque.
